(sec-module-robotics.navigation)=
# Module: robotics.navigation

path planning and navigation of robots with known obstacles: RRT-Connect in joint space with shortcut
smoothing for serial robots, on the collision check in C++ exudyn.cUtilities.CollisionModel (#3383);
an occupancy grid with A* and RRT-Connect in the plane for mobile robots, pure pursuit for a differential drive (#3384)

- **Author**: Johannes Gerstmayr
- **Date**: 2026-11-09

(sec-navigation-jointlimits)=

[`JointLimits(robot, defaultLimits = (-np.pi, np.pi))`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L29)

(sec-navigation-planjointpath)=
## Function: PlanJointPath

[`PlanJointPath(collisionModel, qStart, qGoal, jointLimits = None, margin = 0., maxStep = 0.1, edgeStep = 0.02, maxIterations = 20000, goalBias = 0.1, seed = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L75)

- **function description**: A collision-free path in joint space by RRT-Connect (J. Kuffner, S. LaValle, 2000): two trees grow from the start and the goal, one to a random point and the other as far as it can to the new point of the first. The result is not optimal, see ShortcutPath.
- **input**:
  - `collisionModel`: the exudyn.cUtilities.CollisionModel of the robot and its environment
  - `qStart`: the joint coordinates of the start
  - `qGoal`: the joint coordinates of the goal
  - `jointLimits`: None for -pi to pi, or an array of shape (n, 2), see JointLimits
  - `margin`: the distance which the shapes keep
  - `maxStep`: the largest change of a joint coordinate in an edge of the tree
  - `edgeStep`: the step of the collision check along an edge
  - `maxIterations`: the largest number of random points
  - `goalBias`: the probability of growing towards the root of the other tree instead of a random point
  - `seed`: the seed of the random numbers, for a repeatable result
- **output**: array of the waypoints, one per row, from qStart to qGoal


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotPathPlanningTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotPathPlanningTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-shortcutpath)=
## Function: ShortcutPath

[`ShortcutPath(collisionModel, path, margin = 0., edgeStep = 0.02, iterations = 200, seed = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L130)

- **function description**: A shorter path: random pairs of waypoints are connected directly wherever the straight motion in joint space is free.
- **input**:
  - `collisionModel`: the exudyn.cUtilities.CollisionModel of the robot and its environment
  - `path`: the waypoints, one per row, as returned by PlanJointPath
  - `margin`: the distance which the shapes keep
  - `edgeStep`: the step of the collision check along an edge
  - `iterations`: the number of random pairs
  - `seed`: the seed of the random numbers, for a repeatable result
- **output**: array of the waypoints, one per row, with the first and the last one of path


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py) (Ex), [`robotPathPlanningTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotPathPlanningTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-plantopose)=
## Function: PlanToPose

[`PlanToPose(collisionModel, robot, qStart, HTgoal, jointLimits = None, margin = 0., attempts = 30, seed = None, **options)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L155)

- **function description**: A collision-free path in joint space to a pose of the tool: the free solutions of the inverse kinematics are tried, the nearest to qStart first; further keyword arguments go to PlanJointPath, e.g. maxStep.
- **input**:
  - `collisionModel`: the exudyn.cUtilities.CollisionModel of the robot and its environment
  - `robot`: the Robot
  - `qStart`: the joint coordinates of the start
  - `HTgoal`: the frame of the tool at the goal, exu.HT or 4x4 matrix
  - `jointLimits`: None for those of the robot, or an array of shape (n, 2), see JointLimits
  - `margin`: the distance which the shapes keep
  - `attempts`: the number of random starts of the numerical inverse kinematics, for robots without analytic solution
  - `seed`: the seed of the random numbers, for a repeatable result
- **output**: array of the waypoints, one per row, from qStart to the goal


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py) (Ex), [`robotPathPlanningTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotPathPlanningTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-trajectoryfrompath)=
## Function: TrajectoryFromPath

[`TrajectoryFromPath(collisionModel, path, maxVelocities, maxAccelerations, margin = 0., edgeStep = 0.02)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L194)

- **function description**: A Trajectory through the waypoints of a path, as fast as the limits allow and without stopping at the waypoints where this is free: blending lets the motion cut the corners, so that it is checked and the blend times are reduced if needed; without blending the motion is the path, which is free.
- **input**:
  - `collisionModel`: the exudyn.cUtilities.CollisionModel of the robot and its environment
  - `path`: the waypoints, one per row
  - `maxVelocities`: the largest velocity per joint
  - `maxAccelerations`: the largest acceleration per joint
  - `margin`: the distance which the shapes keep
  - `edgeStep`: the largest change of a joint coordinate between two checks
- **output**: the Trajectory, for Robot.SetControl or Trajectory.Evaluate


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/pathPlanningUR5.py) (Ex), [`robotPathPlanningTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotPathPlanningTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-plangridpath)=
## Function: PlanGridPath

[`PlanGridPath(grid, start, goal, connectivity = 8, clearanceWeight = 0., smooth = True)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L352)

- **function description**: The shortest path on the cells of an occupancy grid by A*. Inflate the grid by the radius of the robot before.
- **input**:
  - `grid`: the OccupancyGrid
  - `start`: the position [x, y] of the start
  - `goal`: the position [x, y] of the goal
  - `connectivity`: 4 or 8, the neighbors of a cell; with 8, a diagonal step needs both neighbor cells beside it free
  - `clearanceWeight`: if > 0, a cell at distance d of an obstacle costs more by clearanceWeight/d per cell, which keeps the path away from the obstacles
  - `smooth`: if True, waypoints are left out where the straight line between the others is free
- **output**: array of the waypoints [x, y], one per row, from start to goal


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotics/mobileRobotsNavigation.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/Examples/robotics/mobileRobotsNavigation.py) (Ex), [`robotNavigationTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotNavigationTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-planse2path)=
## Function: PlanSE2Path

[`PlanSE2Path(shapes, obstacles, start, goal, xRange, yRange, phiRange = (-2*np.pi, 2*np.pi), margin = 0., **options)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L418)

- **function description**: A path of a robot in the plane in the coordinates x, y and the rotation phi by RRT-Connect, for narrow spaces in which the shape of the robot matters and a grid with the radius of the robot would be closed; further keyword arguments go to PlanJointPath, e.g. maxStep and seed.
- **input**:
  - `shapes`: the collision shapes of the robot, in its frame, in a list as for Robot.GetCollisionModel
  - `obstacles`: the obstacles as for Robot.GetCollisionModel
  - `start`: the pose [x, y, phi] of the start
  - `goal`: the pose [x, y, phi] of the goal
  - `xRange`: [xMin, xMax], the range of x
  - `yRange`: [yMin, yMax], the range of y
  - `phiRange`: the range of phi
  - `margin`: the distance which the shapes keep
- **output**: array of the waypoints [x, y, phi], one per row, from start to goal; straight motions in these coordinates are free


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotNavigationTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotNavigationTest.py) (TM)


(sec-navigation-pathwithheadings)=
## Function: PathWithHeadings

[`PathWithHeadings(path, initialHeading = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L444)

- **function description**: The poses of a differential drive along a path in the plane, which turns on the spot at each waypoint: the waypoints twice, with the heading of the segment before and after; a coordinate is a Trajectory waypoint.
- **input**:
  - `path`: the waypoints [x, y], one per row
  - `initialHeading`: None to start in the direction of the first segment, or the heading at the start
- **output**: array of the waypoints [x, y, phi], one per row; phi is continuous, the shorter turn is taken


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`robotNavigationTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/robotNavigationTest.py) (TM)

(sec-module-robotics.navigation-class-occupancygrid)=
## CLASS OccupancyGrid (in module robotics.navigation)

**class description**: A map of the plane in square cells which are free or occupied; a mobile robot is planned as a point on the grid, after the obstacles are inflated by its radius. Attributes: occupied: boolean array, indices x and y


*example*:

```python
  grid = OccupancyGrid([0, 10], [0, 8], 0.05)
  grid.AddRectangle([5, 4], [0.2, 6])
  grid.AddCircle([2, 2], 0.5)
  grid.Inflate(0.3)
  path = PlanGridPath(grid, [1, 1], [9, 7])
```

(sec-module-robotics.navigation-class-purepursuit)=
## CLASS PurePursuit (in module robotics.navigation)

**class description**: The pure-pursuit controller of a differential drive: the robot drives on the arc through a point of the path at the distance lookAhead ahead of it (R. C. Coulter, 1992).


*example*:

```python
  controller = PurePursuit(path, lookAhead=0.3, speed=0.4)
  (v, omega) = controller.Control([x, y, phi])
```


(sec-navigation-purepursuit---init--)=
### Class function: __init__

[`__init__(self, path, lookAhead, speed, goalTolerance = 0.02, maxTurnRate = np.inf)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/robotics/navigation.py#L473)

- **class function description**: create the controller
- **input**:
  - `path`: the waypoints [x, y], one per row
  - `lookAhead`: the distance of the point of the path which is followed
  - `speed`: the forward velocity
  - `goalTolerance`: the distance to the end of the path at which the robot stops
  - `maxTurnRate`: the largest absolute value of the rotation velocity
